title: GroundingPack
description: The machine-readable form of the KGP grounding-pack.md §2 envelope: a content-addressed, self-describing bundle of knowledge scoped to one or more worlds (KINP §5). The envelope is exactly the KGP §2 shape (kgp_version / pack_id / producer / worlds / kind / basis / dialect + entities / assertions / links / provenance / manifest): no hard-coded producer discriminator and no free-string pack id — any KINP namespace may produce a pack, and the pack id is content-addressed (KGP §2.1). Exact on the envelope, ids, provenance, license; permissive on entity fields. This is the KGP §4 JSON encoding — the lossless twin of the canonical TSV, and deliberately NOT a JSON-LD document: per ADR-0006 the RDF-star / W3C PROV / JSON-LD form is a one-directional projection (§4.1) that is never authoritative on ingest, so nothing here depends on a resolvable @context and no koine schema models a projection. The pack — manifest included — is the unit of transfer; a bare projection is not.

kgp_version.description: The KGP spec version (semver) this pack was produced against — e.g. "0.5.0". A producer-local grounding-contract constant is NOT a substitute: every pack declares the koine spec version it conforms to.

pack_id.description: Content-addressed pack id (KGP §2.1): sha256-<hex> of the canonical manifest ⊕ sorted(entities) ⊕ sorted(assertions) ⊕ sorted(links). Byte-reproducible — two producers emitting the same knowledge emit the same pack_id.

producer.description: The producing participant's KINP namespace (identity.md §3.4), e.g. `refkb`, `analyzer`, `worldsim`. Any KINP namespace may produce a pack — this is data, never a fixed discriminator.

worlds.description: The world CURIEs this pack is scoped to (KINP §5), e.g. `refkb:world:consensus-reality`.

kind.description: Directionality (KGP §6): a full `snapshot` or a `delta` applied against `basis`.

basis.description: For kind=delta, the `pack_id` this delta applies against (KGP §6); null for a snapshot.

dialect.description: Pack-level logic dialect (KGP §2 envelope, §5) — the highest logic tier a consumer may evaluate over this pack's assertions. NOT an egress or trust field; local-only is excluded here because it is an egress class, not a dialect tier (KGP §5). The grounding-only floor is deliberately cheap: a SHA-256 implementation, the relation registry and a TSV writer — no graph store, no JSON-LD processor, no context resolution (KGP §3.4, §5).

entities.description: The referenced entity records (KGP §2): each keyed by a `csid` — structurally the KINP entity CURIE (identity.md §7.1) — never a producer-local ad-hoc id.

assertions.description: The KINP assertion envelopes (identity.md §7.1) this pack carries. Each `id` is the content-addressed claim id (KGP §3), so identical claims dedup/merge across producers. Untyped fact strings are NOT the envelope shape — Prolog is a §4 serialization only, as are Datalog, ProbLog, Neo4j, and the RDF-star/PROV/JSON-LD projection (§4.1).

links.description: Equivalence + lifecycle relations (same_as / based_on / part_of / instance_of / retracts / supersedes) — themselves assertions using KINP's reserved relations (identity.md §7.1), so each `id` is a content-addressed claim id.

provenance.description: PROV-*shaped* activities/agents referenced by the assertions (KGP §2, §7). Shaped after W3C PROV but not named in its vocabulary here: the bundle carries no RDF dependency, and PROV terms appear only in the §4.1 projection (ADR-0006).

manifest.description: The self-describing pack manifest (KGP §2): record counts, creation time, optional signing, and the license admission policy (§7.1).

license_policy.description: The license admission allowlist (KGP §7.1): license id -> record count; must cover every record.
